title: Could we have spotted these failures without drawing arcs?
description: For the sets three, four, eight and two, three, six, the longest side is compared with the other two added together. The comparison gives the same answer the arcs gave, with no drawing at all.
teaching_notes: One idea: the longest side compared with the other two added together tells us at once whether a triangle can exist. Watch for children who compare two shorter sides with each other instead of using the longest side.

source: We checked by construction that there are no triangles having sidelengths 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm, and 2 cm, 3 cm and 6 cm. Check if you could have found this without trying to construct the triangle.
video_script.why: The child has seen the arcs fail to meet for two sets and now finds the same result by comparing lengths on paper.
video_script.substitution: In each set the longest side is the direct length and the other two added together are the roundabout length.
video_script.anchor: Two sets of sidelengths, three, four, eight and two, three, six, whose arcs never met
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, neither set makes a triangle, and no construction is needed.

final_answer.value: Yes: 3 + 4 = 7 < 8 and 2 + 3 = 5 < 6, so neither set makes a triangle
final_answer.spoken: yes, neither set makes a triangle, because seven is less than eight and five is less than six

never_show: the words neither set makes a triangle before the answer beat
maths_rules: 3, 4, 8: longest 8; other two 3 + 4 = 7; 8 > 7, the direct length is longer
2, 3, 6: longest 6; other two 2 + 3 = 5; 6 > 5, the direct length is longer
arcs left a gap of 8 - 7 = 1 cm and 6 - 5 = 1 cm
